newsitem.title: UK: British trainee surgeons operate alone - study.
newsitem.headline: British trainee surgeons operate alone - study.

text.p: Trainee British surgeons are regularly operating on patients without supervision, researchers reported on Friday.

Janet Wilson and colleagues at the University of Newcastle said a survey of 276 trainee surgeons and young consultants showed most had done first-time operations without supervision by a more experienced surgeon.
These included hernia repairs, kidney transplants, spleen removals, and removal of the thyroid gland.
In a letter to the British Medical Journal, Wilson said she had asked the 276 surgeons several questions in a postal survey.

"Respondents were asked to indicate whether they had ever undertaken a surgical procedure for the first time 'without your trainer being present in the theatre' (and) to specify any such procedure'," they wrote.
They found 86 percent of general surgeons said they had and 66 percent of ear, nose and throat surgeons.
"Unsupervised first surgery is not ideal training," Wilson wrote.
